reviewer_verdict.verdict: KEEP as proved Gaussian special case; DROP any implication that it establishes P0321
reviewer_verdict.exact_statement: For the stipulated cutoff Gaussian displacement field with transverse covariance aT|k|^-2 PT and longitudinal covariance aL|k|^-s PL (aT>0,aL>=0,0<=s<2), its density-wave surrogate decays as a positive constant times r^-aT|q|²/(4π), and its linearized sixfold orientation surrogate has a positive limiting correlation.
reviewer_verdict.assumptions: Cutoff Lambda>0, q≠0, stationary increments, fixed direction, the orientation observable is curl(u)/2; no Riesz particle identification.
reviewer_verdict.proof_or_counterexample: Independently: angular integration gives π[1-J0(t)-cos(2α)J2(t)] and the radial integral is log r+O(1), so Var(q·Δu)=aT|q|² log r/(2π)+O(1). The curl spectrum is aT/4 on the cutoff disk, hence Var θ=aT Λ²/(16π) and Gaussian characteristic functions yield lim C6=exp(-36 Var θ)>0.
reviewer_verdict.remaining_gap: Transfer from Gaussian elastic field to Gibbs particle process and Delaunay orientational observable, plus defect proliferation yielding fast translational decay. This surrogate itself has algebraic translational decay, so it is not a hexatic phase.
